title: Skip cargo checks that a change's paths cannot affect
summary: Retry of the check-skipping job, fixing its three findings. Checks are skipped only when every changed path is in a configured "cannot affect" list, defined once and shared. Anything unlisted (studies/, *.json, Cargo files, any code) runs all checks, and the run loop is tested.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests for the skip decision and a run-loop test for the skip, answering the minor finding.
The skip rule is enforced by config plus code with tests, not prose.
One focused change to the check runner and its config.
Behavior criteria name cargo test commands the verifier can run.
Decision entry and changelog written for an outside reader.
The retry's intent and failures were recovered from the quoted findings and the repository.

assumptions: Safe direction: a check is skipped only if every changed path matches an inert list; an unmatched path runs the check. This fixes the blocker, where an allow-list of affecting paths missed studies/*.json.

xtask/tests/policy.rs and other tests read docs files (docs/non-rust-files.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/enforcement.md), so those docs, and any file a test reads, must not be inert for the test check. Fmt and clippy can skip on any markdown-only change.
The pattern list is defined once in athena.toml and shared by the change and study capabilities, e.g. a top-level table of named path sets that each check references, not copied per check.
A skipped check is recorded as a passed CheckRun with a note 'not run: no changed path can affect it', as the earlier attempt did, so the record shows the skip.
The nested-run skip stays as is; the new skip is evaluated from the job's change list (ChangeList::paths).
athena.toml is a governance file and changes only governs later jobs; this job's own checks use its base config.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml defines the 'cannot affect' path patterns once, and every check that uses them refers to that single definition; no pattern list appears more than once.
A change touching only studies/**, any .json file, Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, or any .rs file never skips the test check (covered by a unit test of the skip decision).
Docs files that tests read (docs/non-rust-files.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/enforcement.md and any others found by grep for reads in tests) do not allow skipping the test check.
Config parsing rejects or defaults safely: a check with no path set always runs; an empty change list runs every check.

A run-loop test in athena-core shows that a job whose change list is docs-only records a CheckRun with the note 'not run: no changed path can affect it' for skipped checks, and still runs unaffected checks. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A run-loop test shows a studies/*.json-only change runs the test check. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and cargo test --locked pass.
The change is documented: a decision entry in docs/decisions.md and a CHANGELOG.md line; athena.toml is named as a governance deliverable.

out_of_scope: Speeding up cargo itself (caching, incremental builds, shared target dirs).
Changing what the verifier agent runs.
Editing records/ or other governance files (defaults.toml, CI workflows, rust-toolchain.toml).
Skipping the secrets or landing gates.
departures: Cost and time are above the reference because the change spans config, core, and two capabilities, needs run-loop tests, and runs full cargo checks, and the previous attempt failed verification.
